newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 7.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - Beginning today, patients of emergency doctors should no longer have to worry that they will be required to pay in cash for treatment. The Medical Chamber stopped its invitation for doctors to collect cash payments after Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna approved an alternative payment system of 77 crowns per point with limited hours.

- After the bankruptcy of Oasis Tours last week, the travel agency Travela announced bankruptcy on Friday, leaving a few thousand travellers with useless tickets. Others are stranded with no immediate way of returning from holidays.

- Severoceska Energetika (SE) announced yesterday that it would stop supplying electricity to Czech Railways (CD) in 11 places in the north of the Czech Republic today, due to CD's debts of 30 million crowns. Late last night, SE's director announced that due to an agreement with the Industry and Trade Ministry, electricity would not yet be cut off.
- Steady rain throughout the weekend led to floods in Moravia and Slezska, paralyzing transport and causing many residents to leave their homes.

- After two and a half months, the Social Democrats's (CSSD) bank accounts were unfrozen. CSSD covered all its tax debts from 1991 to 1993, and the Financial Office for Prague 1 freed up its accounts.

- Just after 5:00 p.m. on Sunday, several participants in a blockade against the Temelin Nuclear Power Plant got over the gates and entered the construction site. Security agencies were helpless in stopping them.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Nova Hut signed an agreement in Columbia with Spain's Carbomec for the supply of steel mining braces.
- Upon the request of the Bank of New York, the Czech National Bank gave Komercni Banka permission to increase its GDR issue to up to 13 percent of its basic capital.

- The Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) are beginning to prefer an opposition proposal for corporate income taxes to decrease to 29 percent. The party will make a definite decision tonight after a meeting with Finance Minister Ivan Pilip.
- Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka is preparing to issue crown bonds of six billion crowns in the middle of July.

- Komercni Banka expects to open credit links for Ukraine of $60 million within a few weeks. An agreement enabling financing of projects for Czech companies is already signed between Komercni and UKRIN Bank.

- Growth in the M2 money supply, excluding deposits of SPT Telecom, was 6.8 percent year-on-year in May, compared to 6.2 percent in April. Including SPT's deposits, it grew 6.1 percent, compared to 5.3 percent in April.
LIDOVE NOVINY - Parliament approved the cabinet's budget cuts, which should balance the budget for the first quarter of this year.

- Nomura Capital, the Czech branch of Japanese Nomura International, bought 12.58 percent of shares in brewer Radegast from Ia Postovni Banka, according to a report from the Security Centre in Prague.
- Plzensky Pivovar signed a contract for licence production of Gambrinus beer in the Saransk brewery south-east of Moscow, the first entry of the Czech beer industry into Russia without exports.
- From July 1, horses and economic breeding animals can be traded between the Czech Republic and Romania with no customs charge.
- Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl, backed by the Civic Democratic Alliance, intends to propose that the cabinet cancel the import deposit system.

PRAVO - Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka's base rate for credits of up to one year will decrease from today to 18 percent, its rate for credits of one to two years to 17 percent, and its prime rate will be 17.5 percent.
- A music party of about 200 skinheads in Jas cultural centre in Plzen on Saturday was ended prematurely by the police when fights broke out inside.

- On Friday, only three votes stopped parliament from accepting the proposal of Republican Vojtech Filip to call for Klaus to resign due to the crisis in the health system. Filip also failed with proposals for Health Minister Jan Strasky and the director of Vseobecna Zdravotni Pojistovna Jiri Nemec to resign.
